frontMatter.value: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities and present them as a visual report, then grill through the one you pick. Use for 'refactor what next', 'tech debt', 'this repo is a mess, where do I start', or a scoped architecture review.

passages.text: # Architecture survey
passages.reason: The skill's title is its roster name, architecture-survey, which R22 gives the start improve-codebase-architecture became.
passages.gist: Titled architecture-survey, as R22 renamed improve-codebase-architecture

passages.text: Architecture survey is the start for a question about the code's structure as a whole: "refactor what next", "tech debt", "this repo is a mess, where do I start", or a scoped architecture review. Outside an orientation the survey is a report and edits no file of the repository, so it needs no mode and no record: its report lives in the working files, the id a date and a slug as a change's is, deleted when the survey ends without a finding taken up, and a change that takes one up holds the report under its own id. When `architecture-map` (extra, installs on request) has written the map's snapshot, read it before walking the codebase; once a deepening lands, the map's refresh folds it back in. The owner decides what is taken up, and a finding taken up becomes a change under the mode the owner approves. At an orientation, a repository with documents and no change record on any branch, local or remote-tracking, the survey runs before the first change, as AGENTS.md says, and opens a quick record before it writes its result into the knowledge homes the workspace's work guide names; the report itself stays in the working files. Where a change record exists on any branch, the survey is no orientation: it runs only when the request asks for a survey or the owner names it.
passages.reason: The opening in the start's own voice: when the block's situation sends an agent here, that the survey edits no file and keeps its report in the working files, the map read first where the extra has written it, and a finding taken up becoming a change under an approved mode. At an orientation the result goes into the knowledge homes and the report stays in the working files; where a change record exists the survey runs only when asked, since QA runs surveyed as an orientation where a record existed (J-60, the fourth family). Since J-93 S2 the front names greenline's homes and commands by their nouns, their paths and commands on the skill's references page. J-102 S2: at an orientation the survey opens a quick record before it writes its result into the knowledge homes, as every write does.
passages.gist: Opens the survey: working-file report, orientation only where no record exists
passages.ruling: The operator's rulings of 2026-10-04, "cool then lock everything in": a start that edits no file needs no mode and no record, and a finding taken up is a change under the mode the owner approves; R16 of 2026-10-07, a start chosen from the situation a request begins in, a durable output the request did not ask for offered in one line; and R22 of 2026-10-08, "yes amend, with one change", the name architecture-survey and the glossary written at the close step; The operator's card of 2026-10-15 on the QA series, "One fix job after the fifth family", with the delegation of 2026-10-16 whose words finalise the fix job's slices: a start or a habit loads only in the situation its row names, architecture-survey at an orientation and never as one where a change record exists, secrets only with a secret in reach and ponytail before code the request leaves open; a start is named in the record only when it ran; the survey never opens its report; a session with nothing to resume says so and asks for the request; diagnose ranks its hypotheses before the first probe and keeps them ranked; and ponytail builds only on a measured need and reads simplify.md before a refactor; The operator's words of 2026-10-18 on the redesign (N-56, items 2 and 7), "we need the upstream prose upfront and references hold how to work meaning the artefacts etc" and, on the ingest procedures, "we wanna have there prose .. what we don't wanna have is there artefact system and fit them to use ours": a skill's front is the upstream prose its recipe cuts, and greenline's mechanics, where the step's work lands, its section's form, its commands and its depths at each mode, stand on its references page (J-93 S2); The operator's card of 2026-10-21, "A record for every write (Recommended)" (docs/DECISIONS.md, the rows of 2026-10-21): a close asked for by name that writes only to the decisions book, the ADR home or the glossary, and the orientation's survey writing its result into the knowledge homes, each open a quick record first, so the hooks' hold on a workspace while no change is open is one rule with no list of exempt paths

passages.text:
## Handoff

Consumes: the repository; .greenline/map/snapshot.json when architecture-map (extra) has written it (optional); GLOSSARY.md and the decision records
Produces: the offline HTML report under .greenline/tmp/<id>/, never opened, its path told to the owner, copied into the change's folder under .greenline/ledger/<id>/ only when a finding taken up cites it; at an orientation, its result in the knowledge homes; the survey returns to the owner, and a recommendation is not authorization
Next: frame, under the mode the owner approves, for a finding the owner takes up; otherwise none, the survey staying in the reply

# Architecture survey: the practice's mechanics

This page holds where architecture-survey's work lands in the workspace and the commands it runs, which `SKILL.md` names by their nouns. Read it with `SKILL.md` when the work lands in the workspace.
passages.reason: The skill's references page opens: greenline's mechanics for the skill, the paths and commands its front names by their nouns, held apart from the upstream prose since J-93 S2.
passages.gist: Opens the skill's mechanics page, read with SKILL.md

passages.text:
## Where its work lands

The survey's report is `.greenline/tmp/<id>/architecture-review-<timestamp>.html`, in the working files, the id a date and a slug as a change's is; a change that takes a finding up copies it into its folder, `.greenline/ledger/<id>/`. The map's snapshot, which architecture-map writes, is `.greenline/map/snapshot.json`, and the work guide that names the knowledge homes is `.greenline/WORK.md`.
passages.reason: architecture-survey's mechanics: the working files and the change's folder its report lands in, the map's snapshot and the work guide, held apart since J-93 S2.
passages.gist: The report's working files, the change's folder and the map's snapshot
